PAPERS.short: Yang heat anomaly wildfire smoke PM2.5 incident depression All of Us 2026
PAPERS.title: Heat anomaly, wildfire smoke, social-material vulnerability, and incident depression in a national EHR-linked cohort: A preregistered secondary analysis
PAPERS.pm: 30-day mean wildfire-smoke PM2.5 (Stanford ECHO model) at ZIP3
PAPERS.endpoint: First EHR-recorded depression diagnosis
PAPERS.n: Preregistered Cox analysis in All of Us: 179,218 adults free of recorded depression, 5,484 incident cases over a mean 371 days. Exposures were the 30-day pre-index PRISM maximum-temperature anomaly, Stanford ECHO smoke PM2.5 and a social-material vulnerability (SMV) composite. Heat anomaly: HR 1.06 (1.03-1.10) and 1.08 (1.04-1.11) per SD; SMV: HR 1.36 (1.33-1.40) per SD. Mean smoke PM2.5 showed no association in the primary model; secondary smoke metrics were heterogeneous by metric and follow-up window. Limitation: exposure is assigned at the 3-digit ZIP level and frozen at baseline, so smoke-episode contrast is heavily smoothed and a null is weak evidence of no effect; EHR ascertainment depends on care access. Relevance: high - this is the misclassification problem that residence-scale sensor-corrected smoke PM2.5 exists to fix.

PAPERS.short: Lin prenatal air pollution transient tachypnea newborn Taiwan 2026
PAPERS.title: Prenatal air pollution exposure and the risk of transient tachypnea of the newborn
PAPERS.pm: 40-week prenatal PM2.5, CO, NOx from nearest of 71 monitoring stations (postal code)
PAPERS.endpoint: Transient tachypnea of the newborn (TTN)
PAPERS.n: Nationwide matched design on the Taiwan NHIRD linked to the Maternal and Child Health Database, 2004-2020: 3,091 TTN cases in first-born infants and 12,364 controls (1:4 on maternal age, sex, birth date). Exposure over the 40 weeks before birth from the nearest of 71 stations to the residential postal code. Adjusted ORs: CO 1.806 (1.312-2.487), NOx 1.010 (1.005-1.015), PM2.5 1.001 (1.000-1.002), the last per unit concentration with a CI touching the null. Effects concentrated in the Taipei basin. Limitation: nearest-station assignment at postal-code scale, no multipollutant model reported, and the PM2.5 signal is marginal while CO dominates, pointing to traffic as a mixture rather than PM. Relevance: medium - traffic-gradient exposure in a dense basin is where street-level sensor networks change exposure contrast.

PAPERS.short: Gaylord DNA methylation signature prenatal air pollution ECHO cohort 2026
PAPERS.title: A methodology to identify a DNA methylation-based signature of prenatal air pollution exposure in the ECHO Cohort
PAPERS.pm: Prenatal PM2.5, NO2, 8-h max O3 from geocoded ML exposure models
PAPERS.endpoint: Cord-blood DNA methylation classifier of high vs low exposure (AUC)
PAPERS.n: Refines a pipeline that predicts high versus low in-utero air-pollution exposure from cord-blood DNA methylation (450K/EPIC) across multiple ECHO pregnancy cohorts. Exposures were ML-modelled at geocoded addresses; training and validation sets were matched on exposure level, site and array. Validation AUCs: PM2.5 0.64-0.68, NO2 0.62-0.95, O3 0.50-0.75, varying with region, exposure window and the high/low threshold. Limitation: the target is itself a model output, so the epigenetic classifier inherits exposure-model error, and PM2.5 discrimination is modest; dichotomisation discards dose information. Relevance: medium - a biomarker of cumulative exposure is only as good as the exposure surface it is trained on, which is where denser monitoring would raise the ceiling.

PAPERS.short: Perez-Garcia nasal EWAS respiratory biomarkers Mexican American CHAMACOS 2026
PAPERS.title: Nasal Epigenome-Wide Association Study of Respiratory and Allergic Biomarkers in Mexican American Young Adults
PAPERS.pm: Prenatal and past-year PM2.5 and O3 (residential)
PAPERS.geo: USA (Salinas Valley, California, CHAMACOS; Project Viva replication)
PAPERS.endpoint: Nasal DNA methylation vs FeNO, asthma, allergic sensitisation, FEV1/FVC
PAPERS.n: Preprint. Nasal EWAS (EPICv2, 804,220 CpGs) in 354 CHAMACOS young adults aged 22, replicated in 540 Project Viva adolescents aged 13. Forty-nine CpGs were associated with FeNO and 557 DMRs with respiratory outcomes (FDR<0.05); 26 CpGs and 103 DMRs replicated (e.g. LRRFIP1, EPX, IL13). Ten FeNO-related CpGs were associated with prenatal and/or past-year PM2.5 or O3 at nominal p<0.05 only. Limitation: the air-pollution step is a secondary look-up without multiple-testing control, so the PM2.5 link is hypothesis-generating; cross-sectional nasal sampling cannot order exposure and methylation. Relevance: low-medium - an agricultural-valley cohort where PM sources are local and poorly served by regulatory monitors.

PAPERS.short: Wang climate-adaptive city pilot PM2.5 health dividend China 2026
PAPERS.title: Does climate adaptation policy deliver a health dividend? Exposure, modeled health burden, and defensive capacity in China's climate-adaptive city pilots
PAPERS.pm: City-level annual PM2.5 (gridded product), GEMM burden
PAPERS.endpoint: PM2.5 change; GEMM-modelled pollution burden; health-system capacity
PAPERS.n: Difference-in-differences on a 2011-2022 panel of 264 prefecture cities, 21 treated by China's 2017 climate-adaptive city pilot. The pilot is associated with PM2.5 lower by 3.87 ug/m3 (95% CI -6.49 to -1.25; wild-bootstrap p=0.0067); GEMM translates this into an ~8.1% lower modelled burden (-11.32 to -4.76%) - an accounting result, not observed mortality. Defensive-capacity responses (physicians, beds, insurance) are imprecise. Limitation: the estimate shrinks and loses precision in the matched sample and after pollution-convergence adjustment, so selection of already-improving cities is not excluded; 21 treated units is a small base. Relevance: low-medium - policy evaluation at city scale rests on gridded PM2.5 whose own error is not propagated.

PAPERS.short: Musa outdoor air pollution cardiovascular health school children Dar es Salaam 2026
PAPERS.title: Effects of outdoor air pollution on the cardiovascular health of school-aged children residing near polluted areas and the efficacy of mitigation measures in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
PAPERS.pm: None measured; residence near industry, major roads or waste burning used as proxy
PAPERS.endpoint: Elevated blood pressure and cardiovascular symptoms
PAPERS.n: Community cross-sectional study, December 2024-July 2025, of 653 school-aged children living in areas classed as highly polluted by proximity to industrial zones, major roads and waste-burning sites. Single oscillometric BP reading; 19.9% had elevated BP. In log-binomial models, prior respiratory disease carried ARR 8.81 (6.12-12.67) for cardiovascular symptoms. Awareness of mitigation policy was mixed. Limitation: no pollutant was measured and there is no unexposed comparison group, so the title's causal framing is not supported; one-visit BP overstates prevalence in children. Relevance: high as a gap marker - urban East Africa has almost no PM monitoring, and this design shows what health studies look like without it.

PAPERS.journal: Int J Occup Med Environ Health
PAPERS.short: Kobza respiratory ambulatory care air quality Upper Silesia 2026
PAPERS.title: The assessment of respiratory diseases in ambulatory care attributable to air quality in the Upper Silesian agglomeration
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NOx, Pb, benzene from ~50 regional stations
PAPERS.endpoint: Outpatient incidence of pharyngitis, tonsillitis, laryngotracheitis, pneumonia, bronchitis, asthma
PAPERS.n: Five-year ecological analysis correlating daily mean concentrations from about 50 monitoring stations with National Health Fund outpatient incidence for seven respiratory ICD codes across eight regions of the Upper Silesian voivodeship. The strongest signal was for SO2, not PM: tau 0.99 and rho 0.9 in regions 7 and 8, rho 0.78 in regions 1 and 4. Limitation: rank correlations on aggregated series without control for season, influenza, temperature or autocorrelation - seasonality alone would generate these coefficients, so the results carry no causal or PM-specific information. Relevance: low - included because PM2.5/PM10 were analysed; the coal-heating region is a classic case where denser residential PM sensing would sharpen exposure contrast.

PAPERS.short: Waghmare machine learning explainable AI PM2.5 prediction Nagpur 2026
PAPERS.title: Machine learning models with explainable AI for PM2.5 prediction for Urban air quality assessment
PAPERS.pm: Station PM2.5 with co-pollutants and meteorology
PAPERS.endpoint: PM2.5 prediction skill (R2, RMSE, MAE, MAPE)
PAPERS.n: Six regressors (decision tree, extra trees, random forest, KNN, XGBoost, SVR) trained on ~4,000 observations of PM2.5, NO2, SO2, NH3, O3 and meteorology in Nagpur, 70/30 split with 10-fold CV. A single decision tree scored best: test R2 0.90, RMSE 7.5-8.9 ug/m3, MAE 5.4-6.6 ug/m3; SHAP ranked NO2, O3, RH and NH3 top. Limitation: random splits of autocorrelated time series leak information, so skill is inflated; co-pollutants measured at the same station make this a nowcast, not a forecast, and a lone tree beating ensembles is a warning sign. Relevance: low-medium - illustrates the validation discipline (blocked or spatial CV) that sensor-network ML calibration needs.

PAPERS.short: Yousaf nanoscale curvature hygroscopic growth respiratory deposition ultrafine 2026
PAPERS.title: Nanoscale Curvature Controls Hygroscopic Growth and Respiratory Deposition of Atmospheric Nanoparticles
PAPERS.pm: 15-100 nm NaCl particles, HTDMA growth factors fed to MPPD dosimetry
PAPERS.endpoint: Hygroscopic growth factor, DRH and modelled regional respiratory deposition
PAPERS.n: HTDMA measurements of 15-100 nm NaCl particles fed into the MPPD lung-deposition model. The Kelvin effect raised deliquescence RH to 77-81% for 15-36 nm particles and suppressed growth; at 80-90% RH, growth factors were 1.95-2.25 (15 nm) and 1.99-2.36 (100 nm). Ignoring hygroscopic growth overestimated total deposition by up to 25%, with an 18% tracheobronchial difference for particles <=50 nm, and shifted larger UFPs deeper into the lung. Limitation: pure NaCl is a best-case hygroscopic aerosol; ambient UFP is organic-rich with far lower kappa, so the correction is an upper bound. Relevance: medium - the same size-dependent water uptake that biases optical sensors in humid air also changes delivered dose, so dry-size number counts understate the problem.

PAPERS.short: Martin simplified method portable air cleaner CADR low-cost sensors 2026
PAPERS.title: A simplified method for evaluating fine particulate matter removal performance of portable air cleaners
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 decay measured with low-cost sensors vs research-grade instruments
PAPERS.endpoint: Clean air delivery rate (CADR) of DIY and commercial air cleaners
PAPERS.n: Methods paper for community-run CADR testing: release a short-lived nebuliser aerosol in a sealed room, log PM2.5 decay with and without the cleaner on low-cost sensors, and compute CADR from the decay-rate difference. Residential low-cost-sensor CADRs ran ~26% below laboratory values from research-grade instruments - a conservative bias. Of ten units, a four-filter Corsi-Rosenthal box performed best among DIY builds; a fan shroud added ~11%. Across 135 models DIY units cost far less per CADR unit. Limitation: the 26% gap mixes sensor size-response with room mixing and leakage, and is not decomposed; nebuliser aerosol is not wildfire smoke. Relevance: high - a practical protocol in which the low-cost sensor is the reference, with its bias quantified.

PAPERS.short: Wu source-dependent organic aerosol hygroscopicity eastern China biomass burning 2026
PAPERS.title: Source-dependent organic aerosol hygroscopicity in eastern China: observational evidence for conditional enhancement under biomass-burning influence
PAPERS.pm: Humidified light scattering f(RH) with OA composition; ZSR closure for kappa_OA
PAPERS.endpoint: Organic aerosol hygroscopicity parameter kappa_OA
PAPERS.n: Winter field campaign at a rural eastern-China site retrieving organic-aerosol hygroscopicity from humidified nephelometry and ZSR closure. kappa_OA ranged from ~0 to 0.49 (mean 0.11 +/- 0.11) and correlated only weakly with O:C; instead it rose with biomass-burning influence, and ageing enhanced kappa_OA only when biomass burning dominated. Highly oxidised OA under weak biomass influence stayed weakly hygroscopic. Limitation: kappa_OA is a residual after subtracting inorganic contributions, so errors in the inorganic closure load onto the organic term; one site, one season. Relevance: high - humidity correction of optical PM sensors usually assumes a fixed kappa; this shows kappa shifts with source, so smoke-affected periods need a different growth correction.

PAPERS.short: Kalkavouras ammonia sulfuric acid BVOC urban new particle formation Athens 2026
PAPERS.title: Assessing the combined roles of ammonia, sulfuric acid, and biogenic volatile organic compounds in urban new particle formation
PAPERS.pm: Particle number size distributions with NH3, BVOCs and proxy H2SO4
PAPERS.endpoint: NPF frequency, formation rate J14 and growth rate
PAPERS.n: Seven months (June 2023-January 2024) of particle number size distributions, NH3 and BVOCs at the Thissio urban background site in Athens, with a proxy for H2SO4. Mean NH3 2.3 +/- 0.7 ug/m3. NPF occurred on 19% of days, most often in autumn (29-33%) when ventilation and condensation sink were low. Precursor levels barely differed between event and non-event days; the highest J14 came at intermediate NH3 and H2SO4 with low BVOCs, while growth rates rose with NH3 and isoprene/monoterpenes. Limitation: H2SO4 is a proxy, not measured, and the record lacks a full annual cycle. Relevance: medium - NPF bursts dominate urban number concentration but are invisible to mass-based optical sensors, which see nothing below ~300 nm.

PAPERS.short: Schmidt AOD gap filling iterative singular spectrum analysis AERONET Cuiaba 2026
PAPERS.title: Gap filling in long-term AOD time series using Iterative Singular Spectrum Analysis at a tropical AERONET site
PAPERS.pm: AERONET daily aerosol optical depth
PAPERS.endpoint: Reconstruction error of gap-filled AOD series
PAPERS.n: Applies iterative singular spectrum analysis (ISSA) to fill a 2005-2024 daily AOD record from the Cuiaba-Miranda AERONET station, where ~47% of days are missing, mostly in the cloudy wet season. Climatological (day-of-year mean) initialisation beat global-mean initialisation, giving lower error and better temporal consistency, and the cross-validation design materially changed the optimal reconstruction parameters. No error magnitudes are given in the abstract. Limitation: gaps are not missing at random - they coincide with cloud and wet-season aerosol regimes - so a climatology-anchored fill will bias toward dry-season behaviour exactly where data are absent. Relevance: low-medium - the same informative-missingness problem affects sensor networks with humidity-triggered dropouts and satellite-surface fusion.

PAPERS.short: Chakraborty fog intensity droplet size aqueous SOA Kanpur 2026
PAPERS.title: Fog Intensity and Droplet Size-Resolved Aqueous Secondary Organic Aerosol (aqSOA) Formation in Polluted Winter Fog: New Insights from a Combined Observational and Modeling Study
PAPERS.pm: Size-resolved fogwater, offline HR-AMS with PMF; ambient OA
PAPERS.endpoint: Aqueous SOA mass and share of ambient SOA/OA
PAPERS.n: Two winters of size-resolved fogwater at Kanpur analysed by offline HR-AMS and PMF; three highly oxidised factors (O/C 0.95-1.19) were summed as an aqSOA proxy and scaled by liquid water content and WSOC. Across seven events aqSOA was 3.1-8.4 ug/m3, a median ~7% of ambient SOA and 5% of OA, up to 13% of SOA in the densest fogs. Fine droplets carried 43-84% of aqSOA, linked to dissolved Fe and Cu and longer residence. Limitation: the aqSOA proxy is a PMF construct, and offline AMS of fogwater may not represent residual particle mass after evaporation. Relevance: medium - Indo-Gangetic fog episodes are when optical PM sensors fail outright from droplet interference, while secondary mass is being added.

PAPERS.short: Wang carbon footprint air-pollutant emissions Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics 2026
PAPERS.title: Linking Carbon Footprints to Air-Pollutant Emissions from Mega Sporting Events: Evidence from the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics
PAPERS.pm: Co-emitted PM2.5, NOx, SO2, CO, NMVOC from pollutant-to-CO2 ratios
PAPERS.endpoint: Event-attributable air-pollutant emissions and avoided emissions
PAPERS.n: Screening-level inventory converting the verified 713,788 t CO2e footprint of the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics (2016-2022) into co-emitted pollutants via Chinese pollutant-to-CO2 ratios over eight emission carriers, with Shapley attribution and Monte Carlo/Sobol uncertainty. Construction produced 63% of CO2e, ~70% of 1,335 t NOx and 76% of 279 t PM2.5. Green electricity avoided 31% of no-measure emissions; offsets reduced no air pollutant. Limitation: emission-side only - ratio-based PM2.5 with no dispersion, concentration or exposure step, so there is no health quantity, and national average ratios may misstate construction-site fugitive dust. Relevance: low - construction dust is the source class that site-perimeter low-cost PM monitoring is typically deployed to police.

PAPERS.short: He FOXM1 lncRNA COPD-R biomass PM2.5 pulmonary inflammation rat 2026
PAPERS.title: FOXM1/LncRNA COPD-R regulates pulmonary inflammation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease induced by biomass-related PM2.5
PAPERS.pm: Biomass-fuel smoke (rats, 7 months) and biomass-related PM2.5 (L2 cells)
PAPERS.endpoint: lncRNA expression and inflammatory mediators (CCL2, IL-17F, MMP-9, TIMP-1)
PAPERS.n: Rats exposed to biomass-fuel smoke for seven months developed COPD-like disease; lung RNA-seq found 312 differentially expressed lncRNAs (294 up). lncRNA COPD-R rose from 0.15 to 1.05 (relative expression, p<0.01). In rat L2 alveolar cells, biomass-related PM2.5 increased COPD-R; knockdown reduced PM-induced CCL2, IL-17F, MMP-9 and TIMP-1, and ChIP/luciferase assays placed FOXM1 upstream as its transcriptional activator, with rescue experiments consistent with a FOXM1-COPD-R axis. Limitation: whole-smoke exposure in vivo but PM2.5 only in vitro, dose not reported in the abstract, and a rat lncRNA whose human orthologue is not established. Relevance: low - mechanistic support for household biomass PM, where the exposure gap is measurement in homes.

PAPERS.short: Chen pirfenidone fine particulate matter EMT mitochondrial fission autophagy 2026
PAPERS.title: Pirfenidone reduces fine particulate matter-induced epithelial to mesenchymal transition in lung epithelial cells through regulating mitochondrial fission and autophagy
PAPERS.pm: Fine PM (standard reference material type not stated), 100 ug/mL in vitro; intratracheal in mice
PAPERS.endpoint: EMT markers, mitochondrial fission, autophagic flux, lung histology
PAPERS.n: A549 cells exposed to 100 ug/mL fine PM lost E-cadherin and gained vimentin, alpha-SMA, TGF-beta1, Snail and Slug, turned spindle-shaped and migrated more; PM increased mitochondrial fission and LC3B/p62 accumulation, i.e. impaired autophagic flux. Intratracheal PM in mice reproduced EMT markers, inflammatory infiltration and alveolar wall thickening. Pirfenidone reversed these effects in vitro and reduced collagen deposition in vivo. Limitation: 100 ug/mL on a cell monolayer and bolus instillation are far above realistic deposited doses, and A549 is a carcinoma line; the drug result says nothing about population exposure. Relevance: low - mechanism for PM-associated fibrosis; no measurement content.

PAPERS.short: Zakari PM1 microbial profiles lung gut microbiome mice 2026
PAPERS.title: Associations of particulate matter-associated microbial profiles with lung and intestinal microbiomes in healthy mice
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM1 (ions, metals, carbon, oxidative potential, 16S) vs HEPA-filtered and clean air
PAPERS.geo: Not stated in record (ambient-air exposure chamber)
PAPERS.endpoint: Lung and gut 16S microbiome composition; faecal SCFAs
PAPERS.n: Mice were housed under ambient PM1, HEPA-filtered air or clean air; PM1 was characterised for ions, metals, carbon fractions, oxidative potential and its own 16S microbiome (Proteobacteria-dominated). Lung diversity barely changed while the gut microbiome shifted: PM1 reduced Actinobacteriota and Bacteroidota and raised Proteobacteria versus both control arms. Eleven families and six genera overlapped among PM1, lung and gut communities in the PM1 group. Limitation: group sizes and exposure concentrations are not given in the abstract, gases co-vary with PM1, and taxon overlap does not show transfer from air to gut. Relevance: low - airborne microbial load is a PM component no optical sensor resolves.

PAPERS.short: Gautam diesel exhaust miR-133b-3p CTGF Hippo ECM remodeling mouse lung 2026
PAPERS.title: Diesel Exhaust-Induced miR-133b-3p Downregulation and CTGF-Linked Hippo Pathway Inactivation Promote ECM Remodeling and Inflammation in Mouse Lungs
PAPERS.pm: Whole diesel exhaust, 30 min/day, 5 d/week, 8 weeks vs filtered air
PAPERS.endpoint: Lung miRNA expression, Hippo/CTGF signalling, BALF cytokines, MMP/LOX
PAPERS.n: C57BL/6 mice received diesel exhaust 30 min/day, 5 days/week for 8 weeks versus filtered air. Microarrays showed miR-133b-3p down more than 2-fold; CTGF was confirmed as a direct target in A549 cells (mimic reduced CTGF mRNA p=0.0054, protein p=0.0001). In vivo, exhaust raised CTGF, lowered P-YAP/YAP (Hippo inactivation), increased BALF IL-18, IL-1beta and GM-CSF, raised MMP-3/7/12 and lowered LOXL1/4, consistent with ECM remodelling. Limitation: exhaust dose (PM mass, NO2) is not reported in the abstract, so particle and gas effects cannot be separated; the CTGF link is correlative in vivo. Relevance: low - traffic-exhaust mechanism; supports particle number or black carbon over mass as the near-road metric.

PAPERS.short: Yingkar PM2.5-bound PAHs Central Asia urban trends sources risk 2026
PAPERS.title: Environment-to-Health Linkages of PM2.5-Bound Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons in Urban Cities of Central Asia: Trends, Sources, and Risk Assessment
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5-bound PAHs
PAPERS.geo: Kazakhstan (Central Asian cities; inferred from title and author group)
PAPERS.endpoint: PAH trends, sources and health risk
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Yingkar, Omarova, Sovetova, Alibekov et al.). No abstract was retrievable from Crossref or Semantic Scholar at harvest. The title describes trends, source apportionment and health-risk assessment of PM2.5-bound PAHs across urban Central Asian cities - a region with sparse speciation data and heavy coal heating. Cities, sampling design, concentrations and risk estimates are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: medium - coal-heating PAH peaks in Almaty-type basins are where low-cost PM networks already operate without any chemical reference; retry the abstract on a later run.

PAPERS.short: Trivanovic periodic technical inspection particle number devices gasoline exhaust 2026
PAPERS.title: Assessment of existing PN-PTI devices to measure gasoline exhaust
PAPERS.pm: Solid particle number (PN) at tailpipe, PTI-grade counters
PAPERS.geo: Switzerland (inferred from author group; not stated in record)
PAPERS.endpoint: PN-PTI counter performance on gasoline exhaust
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Trivanovic, Melas, Auderset, Hammer et al.). No abstract was retrievable at harvest. The title indicates an evaluation of existing particle-number periodic-technical-inspection (PN-PTI) instruments - developed and type-approved for diesel vehicles with particle filters - when applied to gasoline exhaust, whose size distribution sits lower and nearer the counters' 23 nm or 10 nm cut. Instruments, test vehicles and error magnitudes are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: high - PN-PTI counters are the first mass-produced, low-cost, legally metrological particle counters, and their size-cut behaviour is the same question for community UFP sensing.

PAPERS.short: Fang end of uniformity spatial climatic toxicological redefinitions air quality 2026
PAPERS.title: The End of Uniformity: Spatial, Climatic, and Toxicological Redefinitions of Air Quality
PAPERS.pm: Not stated (perspective on air-quality metrics)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (perspective)
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Fang, Song, Weon). No abstract was retrievable at harvest; the format is likely a viewpoint or perspective. The title argues against uniform air-quality definitions along three axes - spatial heterogeneity, climate-driven change and toxicity beyond mass - which maps directly onto hyperlocal sensing, wildfire-era exposure and component- or oxidative-potential-based metrics. Arguments and any proposals are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: medium - if it advocates spatially resolved or toxicity-weighted standards, it is a policy argument for distributed networks; retry the text on a later run.

PAPERS.short: Hunter e-cigarette aerosol early post-emission particle decay controlled conditions 2026
PAPERS.title: Early post-emission particle decay dynamics of E-cigarette aerosols under controlled conditions
PAPERS.pm: E-cigarette aerosol particle size/number decay
PAPERS.endpoint: Particle decay dynamics after emission
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Hunter, Jacoby, Ferdousi-Rokib, Asa-Awuku et al.). No abstract was retrievable at harvest. The title describes the first seconds-to-minutes decay of e-cigarette aerosol under controlled conditions - evaporation of volatile droplets that shrinks particles rapidly after exhalation or emission. Instruments, conditions and decay constants are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: medium - e-cigarette droplets produce large, short-lived spikes on indoor optical PM sensors that mass-based readings misstate because the particles are liquid and evaporating; useful for indoor network event classification.

PAPERS.short: Spinosa volcanic Saharan dust biomass burning aerosol advections Naples 2026
PAPERS.title: Multiple advections of volcanic, Saharan dust and biomass burning aerosols over Naples
PAPERS.pm: Columnar/profiled aerosol type (likely lidar-based)
PAPERS.endpoint: Aerosol-type advection events
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Spinosa, Manzo, Amoruso, Sannino et al.). No abstract was retrievable at harvest. The title describes overlapping advections of volcanic, Saharan dust and biomass-burning aerosol over Naples; the author group operates lidar there, so a profiling case study is likely but is not confirmed. Instruments, dates and surface PM impacts are not available; nothing is inferred. Relevance: medium - mixed dust/smoke/volcanic layers are the cases where optical low-cost sensors misreport mass most, because refractive index and size change simultaneously.
